title: My 7-day bot leaderboard has a lifetime loser at number 7. So here's the week's best bots with the numbers that don't flatter.
author: QuanTradin
selftext:
Paper desks, my own product, I built it. Here's the week's honest leaderboard.

Seventh place on my 7-day leaderboard this week is a 1-minute momentum rollover bot: 280 trades, up $267 realised. Lifetime it's down $1,421 on 427 trades. Same bot. A seven-day window put a lifetime loser in the top ten.

The desk it sits on tells the same story from the other side. Desk 1 shows floating P&L of +$126,277 on 835 open positions. Realised, all-time: $849. Nearly every dollar of the big number is still open and can go away tomorrow.

So the two rules I've made myself follow when I post a "best bot":
Floating and realised are two different numbers, say which one.
Publish the worst trade beside the win rate.

The actual best bot this week is a premium seller on SPY/QQQ, 177 trades, 73% winners, up $1,281 realised, worst single trade $1,296. The worst bot lifetime is a 15-minute new-highs call buyer, down $6,529 on 41 trades. Both are on the same page, on purpose.
